messages:
ellen: heads up — since the 09:00 rollout we've seen a spike in 5xx from the hosted inference gateway. Customer tickets are coming in for timeouts and 'upstream 502' errors. rolling canary is at 20%. @raj can you check the canary config? :eyes:
raj: on it. saw alerts, graphs look like a sharp jump in 502/504 rates starting ~09:05. can you paste the canary flag set?
ellen: we flipped feature flag `routing:use-pinned-kv-v2=true` and increased canary weight to 20 via deploy console ~09:00. logs show a lot of `HTTP/1.1\" 502` and `context deadline exceeded` in the inference-proxy.
sam: also seeing auth failures from a subset of requests - token validation errors at the gateway layer (401) and then cascade timeouts to backends. but majority are 502/504.
ada: tagged the top customer tickets — some are high-traffic accounts reporting requests hang then fail with 502. support-bot posted ticket IDs: #INC-5121, #INC-5122.
support-bot: customer INC-5121: "Our service started getting 502s after 9am, previously fine. Retry doesn't help." :exclamation:
ops-bot: deploy-bot: canary rollout event: service=inference-gateway, version=2024.11.3, feature=routing.use-pinned-kv-v2, initial_weight=20%.
raj: quick telemetry — p50 latency is normal, but p95/p99 token generation and auth validations spike. I'll tail gateway logs for the canary instances.
raj: tail logs (snip):
```
2025-05-14T09:06:12Z inference-gw-canary-3 host=10.2.4.11 GET /v1/generate 502 "upstream write: broken pipe"
2025-05-14T09:06:14Z inference-gw-canary-2 host=10.2.4.12 GET /v1/generate 504 "context deadline exceeded"
2025-05-14T09:06:15Z inference-gw-canary-3 host=10.2.4.11 POST /v1/embeddings 401 "token invalid"
```
raj: looks like canary instances are failing on long requests, upstream worker pool hitting errors. maybe new kernel path interacts poorly with our batching layer.
sam: could also be kv cache pinning causing memory pressure on canary nodes — OOMs? any OOM traces?
ellen: node metrics for canary instances show increasing GC and CPU at ~09:03, memory usage steady but worker threads blocked. no OOM kills reported.
ada: support update: customers seeing increased billing errors for some requests — likely retries causing duplicate charges. flagged to billing.
raj: reproduction attempt: curl against canary endpoint with header `x-redwood-canary:2024.11.3` and 8 concurrent streams, payload ~1024 tokens. I can reproduce 502 after ~6-8s consistently.
sam: thanks. can you paste the minimal repro?
raj: repro: `for i in {1..8}; do curl -sS -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H "x-redwood-canary: 2024.11.3" -d @prompt.json https://api.redwood-hosted/v1/generate & done` — after a few seconds get 502s and `upstream write` in gateway.
ellen: immediate mitigation: reduce canary weight to 0 and pause the feature flag rollout while we investigate. I'll do the rollback now unless objections.
ada: +1 from support, customers are impacted.
sam: agree. also want to isolate whether it's routing change or kernel/exec change. we should rollback the flag first (simple) then revert canary binary if still failing.
ops-bot: deploy-bot: updated canary weight -> 0% for feature=routing.use-pinned-kv-v2 (actor=ellen).
ops-bot: deploy-bot: rollback action triggered, canary instances are being drained.
raj: after weight -> 0, 5xx rate dropped back to baseline within 90s. p95 latency recovered. Verified no more 502 for the affected customers.
ellen: good. support, please update tickets with rollback note and request customers verify.
support-bot: updating INC-5121/5122: "We rolled back a canary change affecting routing; ask to retry and monitor for further issues."
ada: billing flagged: need to audit charge events for impacted requests — escalated to finance.
sam: follow-up: create a short repro runbook for infra + runtime team, include the exact curl and payload, and add a heap/stack trace capture on canary nodes next time.
raj: initial hypothesis: pinned-kv routing caused uneven request multiplexing under heavy concurrent streaming which exposed a broken path in proxy's streaming write buffer -> backpressure -> upstream broken pipe. another factor: token validation fallback path added in 2024.11.3 may be slower and hold connections.
ellen: action items: [1] runtime/serving: add additional logging in proxy write path and a lock contention trace (owner: sam) [2] infra: add automated canary health gate based on p95/p99 and 5xx diff (owner: raj) [3] support: customer comms and billing audit (owner: nada) [4] product: pause similar flags until we have expanded canary gating (owner: ellen)
ada: I'm opening INC-5123 for billing audit, cc finance.
raj: will schedule a quick standup with runtime team in 30m to prioritize logs and repro.
sam: also recommended backfill synthetic tests that run high concurrency streaming against canary branch.
ellen: thanks everyone. postmortem requested once we have full timeline and root cause. I noted: "rollback at 09:12, impact window 09:03–09:12, customers affected: 4 high-traffic accounts, tickets created."
ops-bot: incident priority -> P2 (service degraded)
ellen: closing loop here — rollback successful, monitoring green, continuous follow-ups in infra runbook. please add any extra notes below. :white_check_mark:
